newsitem.title: USA: U.S. study suggests counselling for Alzheimer cases.
newsitem.headline: U.S. study suggests counselling for Alzheimer cases.

text.p: Nursing home placement for Alzheimer's disease victims can be delayed for nearly a year if those caring for them are given the right kind of education and emotional support, a report said on Tuesday.

"It's encouraging to see scientific evidence that nursing home placement and its financial cost can be delayed when families are enabled to care for their loved ones at home," said Thomas Kirk, a vice president of the Alzheimer's Disease and Related Disorders Association.
The report, published in this week's Journal of the American Medical Association, was based on a study of 209 people who were caring for spouses with the degenerative mental disease.

Some of the group were given six counselling sessions and were told to join support groups. Among members of that group spouses were kept at home for an average of 329 days longer than others who were not given counselling, the report from New York University Medical Centre said.
